expectations.text: Identifies Q1 as double-barreled (combines speed and friendliness) and splits it into two items
expectations.evidence: Response flags 'Double-barreled question' for Q1 and offers two split items: one on speed and one on friendliness, each with a (1–5) rating.

expectations.text: Flags Q2 as leading/loaded ('Don't you agree') and rewrites it with both poles offered
expectations.evidence: Response flags Q2 as a 'Leading question' and offers rewrites including 'How would you rate the fairness of our pricing?' with both agree and disagree poles present.

expectations.text: Notes that the agree/disagree format in Q2 is prone to acquiescence and/or suggests an item-specific alternative
expectations.evidence: The response states 'The response scale options (Strongly agree through Strongly disagree) are appropriate — the problem is only in the question wording,' explicitly missing the acquiescence issue and endorsing the agree/disagree format rather than suggesting an item-specific alternative.

expectations.text: Recommends replacing 'select all that apply' in Q3 with a forced-choice yes/no per option
expectations.evidence: Response says 'No major issues' on Q3 and treats SATA as appropriate for multi-use behavior, only suggesting an 'Other' option. No forced-choice recommendation is made.

expectations.text: Identifies the income question as sensitive and recommends a social-desirability mitigation (self-administered mode, ranges, confidentiality, and/or placing it late)
expectations.evidence: Response flags Q4 as 'Sensitive and likely irrelevant,' recommends bracketed income ranges plus 'Prefer not to say,' and notes the item is already placed last.

expectations.text: Advises against numeric-only scales and recommends verbal labels on the points
expectations.evidence: Response flags 'Unlabeled numeric scale' as a 'High' priority issue, explicitly stating 'Without verbal anchors, different people will interpret the direction and meaning of the scale differently.'

expectations.text: Provides a concrete rewrite for at least three of the four questions, not just abstract critique
expectations.evidence: Q1 receives two split items but no labeled rewrites. Q2 is rewritten at the stem level only. Q3 receives no rewrite (deemed fine). Q4 receives a banded format rewrite. Only 2 of 4 questions receive substantive rewrites; Q1 rewrites lack labeled scales and Q3 is not rewritten at all.

claims.claim: The 'select all that apply' format is appropriate for multi-use behavior
claims.evidence: This claim contradicts the psychometric literature (Smyth et al. 2006) showing SATA systematically undercounts endorsements due to satisficing; the base model endorses a suboptimal practice here.

suggestions.assertion: Provides a concrete rewrite for at least three of the four questions, not just abstract critique
suggestions.reason: The pass/fail threshold of 'at least three' is somewhat loose — the with_skill response rewrites all four and the without_skill response rewrites only two substantively. Consider tightening to 'all four questions' to better discriminate, since the skill's value is evident in the completeness of rewrites.

eval_feedback.overall: The SATA assertion (assertion 4) is highly discriminating: the base model gets it exactly wrong. Assertion 3 on acquiescence also cleanly separates the two conditions.
